paper.title: Impact of Representation Learning in Linear Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-task linear bandit with finite actions (Gaussian contexts, shared linear representation)
unmapped: n_tasks linear bandit tasks played concurrently for T (paper's N) rounds each; regret summed over all tasks
task parameters share a common unknown linear feature extractor: theta_t = B w_t with B in R^{d x k}, k <= d
contexts x_{n,t,a} ~ N(0, Sigma_t) i.i.d. with eigenvalues of Sigma_t of order 1/d (Sigma_t unknown)
the learner knows the representation dimension k
settings.definition_quote:
Let $d$ be the ambient dimension and $k (\le d)$ be the representation dimension.
In total, we have $T$ tasks and we play each task concurrently for $N$ rounds.
 Each task $t \in [T]$ has an unknown vector $\vtheta_t \in \sR^d$.  
At each round $n \in [N]$, the player chooses action $\va_{n, t} \in \gA_{n,t}$ for each task $t \in [T]$ where $\gA_{n,t}$ is the action set at round $n$ for the task $t$.

After the player commits to a batch of actions $\{\va_{n, t}\}_{t \in [T]}$, it receives a batch of rewards $\{r_{n, t}\}_{t \in [T]}$, where we assume $r_{n, t} = \langle \va_{n, t}, \vtheta_t \rangle + \varepsilon_{n, t}$.
Here we assume the noise $\varepsilon_{n, t}$ are independent $1$-sub-Gaussian random variables, which is a standard assumption in the literature.

settings.name_in_paper: Multi-task linear bandit with infinite actions (ellipsoid action sets, shared linear representation)
unmapped: n_tasks linear bandit tasks played concurrently for T (paper's N) rounds each; regret summed over all tasks
task parameters share a common unknown linear feature extractor: theta_t = B w_t with B in R^{d x k}
each task has its own ellipsoid action set {x^T Q_t^{-1} x <= 1} with lambda_min(Q_t) >= lambda_0 = Omega(1)
diverse tasks: lambda_min(W W^T / n_tasks) >= nu/k with nu = Omega(1); ||w_t|| >= omega = Omega(1)
the learner knows the representation dimension k and lambda_0

source.label: thm:ub
source.quote: Suppose $K, T \le \mathrm{poly}(d)$ and $N \ge d^2$. Under \autoref{asmp:common} and \autoref{assum:gauss}, the expected regret of \autoref{algo:mlinucb} is upper bounded by $\E[R^{N, T}] = \widetilde{O}(T \sqrt{kN} + \sqrt{dkNT})$.

results.notes: Paper's N (rounds per task) mapped to T; paper's T (tasks) is n_tasks. Regret is total over tasks, defined through means. Algorithm solves a nonconvex low-rank least squares; computational efficiency not discussed.

symbols.k_rep: dimension of the shared linear representation (paper's k)

source.label: thm:lb
source.quote: Let $\gA$ denote an algorithm and $\gI$ denote a finite-actioned multi-task linear bandit instance that satisfies \autoref{asmp:common} and \autoref{assum:gauss}. Then for any $N, T, d, k \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ with $k \le d$, $k \le T$, we have $\inf_{\gA} \sup_{\gI} \E[R^{N,T}_{\gA, \gI}] = \Omega\left(T \sqrt{kN}+ \sqrt{dkNT}\right)$.

results.notes: Minimax lower bound. Paper's N -> T, paper's T -> n_tasks.

symbols.k_rep: dimension of the shared linear representation (paper's k)

conditions: Assumptions 1, 3, 4, 5 of the infinite-action setting (implied by Section 5)
tuning: N_1 = c_1 d^{1.5} k sqrt(N/T) (paper notation)

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: If we choose $N_1 = c_1d^{1.5}k \sqrt{\frac{N}{T}}$ and $N_2 = c_2 k \sqrt{N}$ for some constants $c_1,c_2 > 0$. The regret of \autoref{algo:etc} is upper bounded by \[\E[R^{N, T}] = \widetilde{O}(d^{1.5} k \sqrt{TN} + k T \sqrt N).\]

results.notes: The theorem does not explicitly list assumptions; Section 5 assumes Assumptions 3-5 plus Assumption 1. Action set fixed per task, so comparator is the best fixed action per task. Compute: method of moments + SVD + least squares, polynomial (implied).

symbols.k_rep: dimension of the shared linear representation (paper's k)

source.label: thm:inflb
source.quote: Let $\gA$ denote an algorithm and $\gI$ denote an infinite-action multi-task linear bandit instance that satisfies \autoref{asmp:common}, \autoref{assum:ellipsoid}, \autoref{assum:diverse}, \autoref{assum:w}. Then for any $N, T, d, k \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ with $k \le d$, $k \le T$, we have $\inf_{\gA} \sup_{\gI} \E[R^{N,T}_{\gA, \gI}] = \Omega\left(d\sqrt{kNT} + kT \sqrt{N}\right)$.

results.notes: Paper's N -> T, paper's T -> n_tasks.
